headline: Election pay ordinance adopted; $120,000 cemetery truck and $9,000 EV charger grant approved; 287 Crescent Street application withdrawn.
summary: The council held four public hearings. Two license requests and the 101 Elm Street car wash permit went to committee, and the 220 Moody Street special permit hearing was continued. The council also approved a $120,000 cemetery truck, two grants, and a new election pay ordinance.
decisions: Referred the second-hand dealer's license for 1275 Main Street for Hits and Hollows to the Licenses and Franchises Committee.
Referred the second-hand dealer's license for 550 Winter Street for Roadshow Concepts LLC to the Licenses and Franchises Committee.
Referred the special permit modification for 101 Elm Street to the Ordinance and Rules Committee and recessed the public hearing to December 14, 2026.
Continued the special permit hearing for 220 Moody Street to December 14, 2026.
Recommended councilors to serve on the Hockey Rink Design Committee, and placed the mayor's request on file.
Referred the $42,536 transfer request for preliminary bridge repair design to the Finance Committee.
Referred the $56,760 funding request for Chester Brook culvert work at Beaver Street to the Finance Committee.
Referred the $40,000 funding request for professional services to the Finance Committee.
Approved 10 resolutions honoring retiring firefighters.
Confirmed the appointment of Richard Pizzi Jr. as a permanent member of the Waltham Council on Aging, 12 in favor.
Confirmed the appointment of Marsha McCleary as a permanent member of the Waltham Council on Aging, 12 in favor.
Approved a $120,000 appropriation from the cemetery sale of lots and graves account for a new truck for the cemetery division.
Approved acceptance of a $52,152 grant from the Office of Grants Research for the FY 2027 municipal road safety program.
Approved acceptance of a $9,000 grant for new EV chargers in the city's public parking lots.
Adopted the compensation ordinance for personnel costs associated with the election, 12 in favor.
Tabled the $462,755 loan order for design of the fire administration wing at the police station, after a first reading.
Approved the fortune teller license at 24 Crescent Street for Manu Park.
Approved the extended hours renewal at 12 Harvard Street for a CVS pharmacy.
Approved the McDevitt 8th grade civics resolution, along with a request for solar trash and recycling compactors on Moody Street.
Approved the National Grid 1725 petition at 205 Second Avenue.
Approved the National Grid 1725 petition at South Street and Vernon Street.
Granted leave to withdraw without prejudice the application to amend the special permit at 287 Crescent Street, 12 in favor.
discussion: 101 Elm Street car wash: Members asked how the new automatic pay stations would affect traffic, whether the site could stay open during construction, and how water runoff and cracked sidewalks could be fixed. Answers were requested for committee.
Trading card store license: A representative said the business wants a second location with more space for players, to buy, sell, and trade sports and trading cards.
Early voting and election day: The council was told early voting runs through Friday at the Malone Archive Center, and election day is Tuesday, November 3rd, with polls open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.
550 Winter Street license: A representative said the company wants an annual license to hold a regular monthly schedule of appraisal and evaluation events.
